content: The management of type 2 diabetes often necessitates a combination therapy approach due to the progressive nature of the disease. Achieving sustained glycemic control over time frequently requires the sequential addition of pharmacological agents. Initial treatment typically begins with metformin as the first-line therapy. However, as the disease advances and the patient’s glycemic targets are no longer achieved with metformin alone, additional medications are usually introduced to preserve therapeutic effectiveness and maintain optimal blood glucose levels.
